D.t: Jermaine Johnson trails by 6.8 and wins 16% of simulations. Closing it takes about 69,335 voters switching sides, or 138,671 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +15.3 and D +2.0. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +10.7. Your best recent poll is On Point Polling at R +8.2; your worst is Trafalgar Group (R) at R +14.9. 5 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Richland, a projected net 75,415 votes; Charleston, a projected net 33,213 votes; Orangeburg, a projected net 12,621 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: York, R +7.8, 5.7% of the vote; Berkeley, R +3.9, 4.3% of the vote; Beaufort, R +5.4, 4.1% of the vote; Dorchester, R +1.6, 3.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jermaine Johnson runs furthest behind in Pickens, Oconee, Anderson. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 65% of voters, 46 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.25 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 58% of voters, 53 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.88 points; Voters without a degree, 56% of voters, 47 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.80 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Jermaine Johnson: Immigration voters 16 to 84, White voters 32 to 66, Voters who can afford daily costs 38 to 62. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$136K cash against $1.7M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Cash: $1.7M in the bank against $136K for Jermaine Johnson.
